trailheadDirection: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 55 miles to the end of the highway. At Heather Meadows go one-way around Picture Lake past the ski lifts; the large parking area is at the end of the road on the right. The highway is plowed only to Heather Meadows outside roughly July to late September.
unverifiedNote: Current-year snow opening date not confirmed.

trailheadDirection: From Index on US-2, turn north onto Index-Galena Road (FR-63) and drive about 16 miles, bearing left at the junction for the final 2 miles of bumpy gravel. Bear left again at the second fork and climb a short hill to the parking area.
unverifiedNote: Sources disagree on whether the 16 miles includes the 2 gravel miles; a WTA closure notice concerns Beckler River Road (FR-65) on the Skykomish side, not this Index approach.

trailheadDirection: From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east 42.1 miles; the trailhead is on the south side of the highway just before Washington Pass Overlook. From Winthrop it is 31.3 miles west, a little under a mile past the overlook. SR-20 closes for winter.

From Marblemount, leave SR-20 onto Cascade River Road (FR-15) and drive to milepost 22.5, where a small pullout is on the left opposite Johannesburg Mountain. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel; the road can close at the Eldorado parking area at milepost 20.
unverifiedNote: Current gate status not confirmed; WTA lists no closure.

trailheadDirection: From Newhalem, drive SR-20 east to between mileposts 141 and 142; the trailhead lot is on the left. SR-20 is closed for the winter season east of Ross Dam.
unverifiedNote: Only a forum post gives the milepost; not confirmed by an official page.

trailheadDirection: From Winthrop, drive SR-20 west about 18 miles to FR-5310-200, about half a mile east of the Klipchuck Campground turnoff. The trailhead is near the gravel pit at the end of that road.
unverifiedNote: Single listing for a Cedar Creek Trail; not confirmed that this is the trailhead used for North Gardner; SummitPost comment from 2010.

trailheadDirection: From Trout Lake, drive Mount Adams Road north to the V intersection with FR-23, veer right and go about 1 mile, then turn left onto FR-80 (signed South Climb) and follow it to its end. Turn right onto FR-8040 and drive north past Morrison Creek Campground to the old Cold Springs Camp; the last 3 miles are very rough and narrow.
unverifiedNote: No closure mentioned; confirm with the ranger district.

trailhead: Cutthroat Peak Climbers Trail Pullout (Hwy 20, ~1.5 mi W of Washington Pass, north side)
trailheadDirection: Drive SR-20 to Washington Pass and continue west about 1.5 miles to a long, wide pullout beside the highway, which is the climbers' parking. SR-20 closes for winter.
unverifiedNote: Sources disagree on which side of the highway the pullout is (north vs south); no named start town given.

trailheadDirection: Drive Chilliwack Lake Road in British Columbia about 30 miles to the Depot Creek Road turnoff, which is about 100 yards before the gated steel bridge over Depot Creek. Depot Creek Road is very rough and overgrown (high-clearance 4WD) and ends at a major washout about 1.7 miles in, where you park.
unverifiedNote: Start town on the Canadian side is not given by the sources; the main trip report is from 2004 and a second dates to about 2020; the road is blocked by the washout itself. Lowered on review: the newest source is about 2020, too old to state the state of a washed-out road.

trailhead: Depot Creek Road washout (via Chilliwack Lake, BC)
trailheadDirection: Drive Chilliwack Lake Road in British Columbia about 30 miles to the Depot Creek Road turnoff, which is about 100 yards before the gated steel bridge over Depot Creek. Depot Creek Road is very rough and overgrown (high-clearance 4WD) and ends at a major washout about 1.7 miles in, where you park.
unverifiedNote: Start town on the Canadian side is not given by the sources; the main trip report is from 2004 and a second dates to about 2020; the road is blocked by the washout itself. Lowered on review: the newest source is about 2020, too old to state the state of a washed-out road.

trailhead: Dingford Creek / Middle Fork Snoqualmie Trailhead
trailheadDirection: From I-90 near North Bend, take exit 34, turn left onto 468th Street and follow it to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road. Go 12 miles to the large Middle Fork parking area, pass it, and turn right onto a gravel road just after the large concrete bridge, signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap. Follow it 6 miles over potholes to a gate, with the trailhead just past it.
unverifiedNote: Exact parking position relative to the gate not confirmed.

trailheadDirection: From Quilcene, drive US-101 south 15 miles and turn west at the large sign for the Duckabush Recreation Area. Continue about 6 miles (the pavement ends after 3.6 miles, and Collins Campground is near 5 miles), and just past the horse parking area bear right and uphill onto FR-2510-060, which is poorly signed; the trailhead is 0.1 mile up.
unverifiedNote: No closure listed.

trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east to milepost 138, where the East Bank trailhead parking is beside the highway. SR-20 is closed for winter beyond Colonial Creek.
unverifiedNote: Pages give only the milepost; side of road not stated.

trailheadDirection: From Marblemount, drive SR-20 east about 45 miles and turn right between mileposts 151 and 152 onto the signed Easy Pass road, which leads to the trailhead lot.

From Marblemount, turn off SR-20 onto Cascade River Road and drive about 20 miles to a large parking area on the right at milepost 20. The first 10 miles are paved and the rest is rough gravel; the road has been closed at this lot for repairs and in winter.
unverifiedNote: Current gate status not confirmed; not a Inspiration-Traverse-specific page.

trailhead: Esmeralda Basin Trailhead (North Fork Teanaway Rd)
trailheadDirection: From Cle Elum, take I-90 exit 85 and drive SR-970 east about 7 miles, then turn left onto Teanaway Road. Bear right as it becomes North Fork Teanaway Road, stay right at the fork signed for trail 1394, and drive about 1.7 more miles to the trailhead.
unverifiedNote: A WTA note dated 12.19.25 says the area was inaccessible due to closures of FR-9737 and nearby roads; current status unconfirmed. Forest Service mileages differ from WTA.

trailhead: FR-6220 / Anderson Creek drainage (no maintained trail)
trailheadDirection: From US-2 about 6 miles east of Gold Bar, turn onto FR-62 (Proctor Creek Road) and drive about 3.3 miles to an unmarked junction. Take the left fork onto FR-6220, which is in poor condition, to the end-of-road parking; the gate at US-2 is sometimes locked.
unverifiedNote: Directions are for the Mount Persis trailhead; no source names an Anderson Creek access specifically. Lowered on review: the drive is to the Mount Persis road end, which is not shown to be the Anderson Creek access.

trailheadDirection: From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32. After 1.3 miles take the left fork onto Ruth Creek Road and continue 5.4 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.

From Bellingham, drive SR-542 east about 46 miles, which is 13 miles past Glacier, and just before the third crossing of the Nooksack River turn left onto FR-32. After 1.3 miles take the left fork onto Ruth Creek Road and continue 5.4 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.

After 1.3 miles take the left fork onto Ruth Creek Road and continue 5.4 miles to its end at Hannegan Campground, where the trailhead is.

From Mazama, head north on Lost River Road and after about 9 miles turn right onto FR-5400. Climb about 8.7 miles to Harts Pass; the road is narrow and rugged, suited to high-clearance vehicles only, and is typically open July through September.
unverifiedNote: Another guide numbers the Lost River stretch differently (9140).
High Bridge is in the Stehekin valley; it has no road connection, and no drivable route was found.

trailhead: Hoh Rain Forest Visitor Center / Hoh River Trailhead
trailheadDirection: From Forks, drive US-101 south about 13 miles and turn east onto Upper Hoh Road. Follow it about 18 miles to the visitor center and trailhead at the end of the road.
unverifiedNote: Upper Hoh Road was closed at milepost 9.7 from December 2024 until May 2025 and briefly in August 2025; no 2026 status found.

trailheadDirection: From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.
From Trout Lake, drive FR-23 north about 24 miles to the junction with FR-2329, signed for Takhlakh Lake Campground. Follow FR-2329 past the campground for about 4.5 miles to the trailhead.

From Gold Bar, drive US-2 east about 7 miles, and just as the road curves left to a large bridge over the Skykomish River turn right onto Mount Index Road. After a quarter mile on dirt, turn right at the sign for the Lake Serene trail; the parking lot is about 500 feet ahead.

From Elbe, drive SR-706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance of the park, then continue about 6.5 miles to Longmire. The center is in the Longmire Administration Building, across from the museum.
unverifiedNote: Directions from archived park page; winter tire-chain requirement applies.

trailheadDirection: From US-101 near Sequim Bay State Park, turn west onto Louella Road, then left onto Palo Alto Road. After about 6 miles turn right onto FR-2880, then in about 1.7 miles turn left onto FR-2870 and follow it to the Upper Dungeness trailhead.
unverifiedNote: Trail 816 leaves from the Dungeness River trail near the Upper Dungeness trailhead; no page gives a trailhead named for Trail 816 itself.

trailheadDirection: From Stevens Pass, drive US-2 east 11.3 miles and turn north onto FR-657, signed for Merritt Lake. Follow it 1.6 miles to the road's end and trailhead parking.
unverifiedNote: Rough, bumpy gravel; distance from Leavenworth differs slightly between sources.

trailheadDirection: From Cle Elum, drive SR-903 north 17 miles past Lake Cle Elum and turn left onto Road 4600 (Cooper Lake Road). Drive Road 4600 about 7 miles over Cooper Pass, then stay on Road 4600 about 3 miles down to the small signed trailhead.
unverifiedNote: WTA reports the trail closed by the Three Queens Fire (note dated 7.30.26); the road is not stated as closed.
